_: Lead fit: would this company buy what the owner sells. Clef picks from these lists and returns calibrated probabilities, it writes no text. Tune the lists to your own services in a fork; a changed list changes the input hash, so companies are asked again.
_buyer: How likely the company is to pay an outside developer, lowest first. Stored on companies.fit as 0 to 100; the score weighs it by level (rules: companies.modelFit).
buyer: no: a large company with its own engineering department, an investor or fund, a public body that only buys through tenders, or a field to avoid (gambling, casino, adult, forex, crypto speculation)
unlikely: builds software itself and rarely hires outside, or there is nothing to build for it
possible: could use outside development help, but nothing in the record points at a need
likely: a small team or business with something to build, fix or automate and no large in-house team, or an agency that subcontracts work to freelancers
_services: Which service fits best. Keys are stored on companies.fit_service.

services.website: a new or rebuilt website, landing page or online store for a business
services.mvp: build a product or MVP from scratch: front end, back end, payments, deploy
services.ai: add AI features to a product: LLM features, agents, chat or answers over its own data
services.automation: automate business processes: integrations between tools, bots, internal dashboards
services.optimization: make an existing product faster, cheaper or more reliable, or fix a product that does not hold load
services.white_label: white-label or subcontract development for an agency's own clients

_stages: What stage the company is at. Keys are stored on companies.fit_stage.

stages.idea: pre-launch or pre-seed: an idea or a prototype, no product live yet
stages.early: launched, small team, early customers or a seed round
stages.growth: growing fast, raised a Series A or later, hiring
stages.established: an established business or agency running for years
